ledger.summary: Leaving the Sage's house (Ralph walking so the Sage can ride), Ralph and Ursula have a lovers' misunderstanding and reconcile. The Sage leads them through rugged high hills and deep valleys full of wild beasts (lions heard), along streams and twice over mountain necks, to a grassy valley with sweet chestnuts at dusk. He has them build a big fire against lions and says he will deal with the Utterbol riders. At night he makes signs, covers the lovers with his cloak and stands between the horses. Twenty-odd riders under the Lord's nephew and Otter arrive, but see only two grey stones, a skeleton leaning on the tree and old horse bones; the frightened nephew flees. Otter, lingering, says he is glad, would rather ride with Ralph than serve "the Devil and his Nephew", and follows.
ledger.geography_notes: Beyond the Sage's high ground: level wood, then thinning trees and broken ground, then very rugged high hills and deep valleys full of wild beasts, crossed by winding routes along streams and twice over mountain necks. At dusk, a small grassy valley with a bush-edged stream and big sweet chestnuts.
